historical_claim_versions.statement: Adversarially audit, verify, or refute OpenAI Manuscript Family 075 (The $`L\log L`$ Fourier-convergence conjecture.; papers: Almost-everywhere Fourier convergence in L log L; Lean status: Partially/Comparator formalized (lean/docs/075.md)): either (a) discover and certify an explicit mathematical flaw, sign/orientation error, counterexample to an intermediate lemma, or statement-fidelity/citation gap with a deterministic symbolic/computational certificate (`verify.py` + `exact_certificate.json`), or (b) independently verify, repair, or generalize the manuscript's core mathematical theorem with a standalone machine-checkable certificate certified by the independent Reviewer.

Under the hypotheses of lemma:compression there is a finite refinement W and index j with G_1(empty)-G_1(W) <= C D_*^2/(E h^2) and K_{m_{j,1}}(W;r_j) <= K_{m_{j,0}}(W;r_j)+E, for a numerical constant C.

Universal two-level finite-search theorem: ordered bounded state coordinates, monotone refinements, positive-minimum clipped offers, and the explicit scalar skip-parameter inequalities imply discovery in finitely many updates with normalized cost at most 2 alpha_1 + 2 alpha_0 <= 4 alpha_1, without assuming decreasing interval widths or exact target decreases.
For all finite contexts, the Section 03 quantities G_s and I_r have the index, refinement monotonicities and common D_* bound asserted in entropy-foundations:context-bounds.
The full and partial block observations satisfy entropy-refinement:one-letter-loss and eq:source-4, including the at-least decrease for Bernoulli partial observations.

If the desired K inequality fails, some full observation has a_j decrease d >= eta=tau/(2m_*) and cost <= 2 p_j d; any target 0<x<=d is available with actual decrease at least x and cost at most 2 p_j x.
The Section 04 ranges are disjoint and descending in j, their row counts strictly increase, and all their endpoints and row counts lie in the domain of the contextual bounds.

For sufficiently large d, the explicit n,N,q_*,u,alpha_0,alpha_1,delta_0,delta_1 satisfy the scalar inequalities used in the two-level search, there is room for the partition, and 4 alpha_1 <= C/h^2 for numerical C.

historical_claim_versions.statement: The full entropy compression lemma:compression follows after the finite search and the separately unverified common-phase extraction and contextual foundations.
The depth- and modulation-uniform delayed Haar estimate prop:dyadic holds under its stated bounded nonnegative input, stopping, and multiplier hypotheses.
Theorem thm:good-set: for mass-one nonnegative rho bounded by exp(d), the integral over {M rho <= exp(4h)} of sup_N |S_N rho| is at most C d.
Theorem thm:main: every complex-valued L log L function on the circle has its symmetric Fourier partial sums converge to it almost everywhere along the full sequence.
The post-search freezing, noisy atom, common phase region, and pruning arguments in Section 04 imply the uniform-in-v conclusion of lemma:compression.
Lemma entropy-foundations:thinning: K_m(W;r)<=C E under its stated m,r hypotheses for every finite refinement W.
The thermal positivity, spectral update, regular evidence, and live budget results of Sections 05-06 hold under their stated hypotheses.
The Section 07 capture, edge charge, and snapshot results hold under their stated hypotheses.
The scalar and vector delayed-path estimates in Section 08 hold with their stated predictability and stopping hypotheses.
The translation and scale averaged kernel calculation and limiting steps in Section 11 transfer prop:dyadic to thm:good-set.
The endpoint layer summation and density argument in Section 11 transfer thm:good-set to the full complex-valued L log L Fourier convergence theorem.

For every preordered state model with bounded ordered coordinates, refinement-monotone costs and endpoints, and positive-minimum partial offers allowing arbitrary actual overshoots, the explicit two-level scalar hypotheses imply finite discovery before N*q*n indices at cost at most 2*alpha_1+2*alpha_0<=4*alpha_1. The source also proves these scalar hypotheses for the manuscript logarithmic parameters when t>=1, exp(t)>=4, ell>=5t, n=exp(ell), N=exp(t), and 2t^2<=q<=2t^2+1.
